items.title: NEW — `bind_each`/`bind_each_by` keep the LIVE list as `row_items` (`row_items.write() = list`, and the effect's `list` is the cell's storage), so an in-place `remove`/`insert` through `SignalCell::update` shrinks it under `row_keys` and `reconcile` panics at `old_items[index]` (kolt channel.vl:54: `index out of bounds: the length is N but the index is N`); an in-place element write leaves the row silently STALE (the reconciler compares the mutated array with itself and Keeps)
items.discussion: the owner's kolt find (2026-09-06); reproduced under the ui_rows DOM stub on 757d3f4b; std, not user-land — `update` + `remove` is the documented idiom; B256 is the seam that lets the alias out, B257 the sibling
items.body:
Two symptoms from one alias. `bind_each` (browser/ui.vl) stores the effect's `list` into `row_items` and later hands `row_items.read()` to `reconcile` beside `row_keys.read()` (a separate list built by `next_keys.push(key(item))`). `SignalCell::update` mutates the storage in place and notifies; the effect then reconciles a `row_keys` of the OLD length against an `old_items` that is the new array itself. For a `remove(0)` on six rows: `same(old_items[5], item)` reads past the end — `index out of bounds: the length is 5 but the index is 5` from `__at` (seven rows give the owner's 6/6). For `messages[0] = Message { .. }` through `update`: `old_items[0]` IS the new element, `same` says Keep, and the row never re-renders (DOM-stub repro: the tree still shows the old text, no `render` line). `bind_each_by` holds `row_items` the same way (its `same` is constant, so only the panic applies). The list-`set` path is untouched: a fresh array replaces the storage and the old one stays whole.

Interim std fix: snapshot what the binding keeps (`row_items.write() = list.map(|x| x)` or a `List` copy intrinsic) — O(n) per change, which the keys pass already pays. The principled fix is B256 (a `Shared::read()` result that obeys rule 1), after which `list` itself is a copy and the snapshot is redundant. Pin both symptoms in `ui_rows.rs` (one `update`-driven `remove`, one in-place element write) — the only existing pin that drives `update` beside a `bind_each` (`reactive_lifetimes.rs`'s cycle exemplar) only PUSHES, which happens to survive (a longer `old_items` is never read past `old_keys`).

Kolt workaround until then: replace instead of mutate — `self.messages.set(self.messages.get().filter(|m| !m.eq(message)))`; verified to reconcile cleanly and keep every surviving row's element.

items.title: NEW — `Shared::read()` hands out the cell's STORAGE: `SharedValue` lowers to the bare slot `self.v` though the intrinsic table says "a copy of the cell's value" and spec §6.1 says a value-returning signature copies; the clone pass exempts every call ("calls own their result"), so `let b = h.read()`, `mut c = h.read(); c.push(x)` and `SignalCell::get()` all alias the cell (`c.push` grows the cell)
items.discussion: found under B255 (2026-09-06); the seam that lets `bind_each`'s alias out and makes `update`'s in-place mutation observable through every earlier `get()`; the owner's call on WHERE the copy lives
items.status: OPEN — found under B255 (2026-09-06); a ruling wanted
items.body:
Probe on 757d3f4b (`assign.vl`): `let b = h.read(); h.write().push(9)` — `b` reads 5; `mut c = h.read(); c.push(10)` — the CELL reads 6. Emitted: `const b = h.v; let c = h.v;` — no `__clone`. `compute_clone_sites` copies only PLACES (`is_place_expr`: a local or a field) and leaves calls alone on the premise the spec states in §6.1 ("a call owns its result"); `SharedValue` is a call that returns storage, so the premise is false at exactly this intrinsic, and `SignalCell::get()` (`self.value.read()`) inherits it. `Shared`'s header comment says binding shares the CELL — that is the handle; the VALUE read out is declared `read(self): T`, a value return, which §6.1 says copies ("a signature that hands back a value hands back a value"; only a `borrows` projection names storage).

Two fixes, and which one is the owner's ruling: (a) `SharedValue` emits `__clone(self.v)` — every read of a list/map/struct deep-copies, including `bind_each`'s three `read()`s per effect and every `for x in cell.read()`; simple, and the cost wants measuring on kolt's client leg before it lands; (b) the clone pass treats a `SharedValue` result (and `get()`, a call returning one) as a PLACE: a binding, assignment, construction slot or `own` argument fed by it copies, a temporary (`for item in cell.read()`, `cell.read().len()`) stays free, and rule 2's liveness elision cannot fire because the source is not a local — rule 1's cost only where two owners come to exist. My recommendation is (b). Either way the intrinsic-table comment and `shared.vl`'s doc ("project the cell's value") should say the same thing the emission does.

items.title: NEW — ASSIGNMENT from a live aggregate place does not copy: `b = a; a.push(4)` leaves `b` at 4, `r = q; q.x = 10` leaves `r.x` at 10 (lists and structs alike), while the binding form `mut f = e` clones — spec §6.1 names assignment first and its own example fails rewritten as one
items.discussion: found under B255 (2026-09-06); miscompile class — a program that reads a copied aggregate after mutating the source computes the wrong value; `compute_clone_sites`' Assignment arm does `consider` the value, so one of its inputs declines
items.body:
Probe on 757d3f4b (`assign3.vl`): P1 `mut b = [0]; b = a; print(a.len()); a.push(4)` — `b` reads 4 with `a` read AFTER the assignment, so this is not rule 2's last-use elision; P2 `r = q; q.x = 10` — `r.x` reads 10; P3 with a dead source — elision legitimate; P4 `mut f = e; e.push(4)` — `f` reads 3 (`let f = __clone(e)`). Emitted for P1/P2: `b = a;` / `r = q;` with no `__clone`. The same miss covers assignment THROUGH a view: `h.write() = c; c.push(4)` grows the cell (`h.v = c;`), which is how `bind_each`'s `row_items.write() = list` came to alias (B255).

The Assignment arm calls `consider(value_id, self.type_id_of_expr(value_id))` where the `let` arm passes the variable's own type and the construction arms `place_value_type_id`; `consider` also asks `is_elidable_copy` (liveness) and `assignment_target_is_view`. Find which input declines for a plain local on the right of `=` and pin the four probes as a rule 1 pin in `inference/borrows.rs` (P1, P2, and the `h.write() = c` form, with P3 asserting the elision still fires when the source is dead).

items.title: NEW — `List::remove`/`List::insert` are hand-written shift loops over the checked subscript helpers (`__at`/`__at_put` per element); lowered over the native `splice` (an intrinsic beside `pop`), with the bounds panic KEPT, they cost 8–29× less CPU on a 10k list and the same on a 6-element one
items.discussion: the owner's question while migrating kolt (2026-09-06); measured in node 24 with `process.cpuUsage`, loadavg 0.03
items.body:
Per-op CPU (µs), hand loop → `splice`, ten thousand elements: `remove(0)` 4.71 → 0.56; `insert(0)` 6.81 → 0.59; `remove(mid)` 5.53 → 0.19. One thousand: 0.51 → 0.21, 0.68 → 0.27, 0.55 → 0.11. Six elements: 0.01 either way (a native call costs what six checked loads cost). The loop pays a bounds check per moved element and cannot be vectorized; `splice` is one `memmove`.

Shape: `external fun remove(&mut self, index: i32): T` / `insert(&mut self, index: i32, own value: T): void` as intrinsics in `pop`'s pattern, each emitting a helper that keeps `[]`'s panic — `splice` CLAMPS an index past the end (returns `[]`, inserts at the end) and reads a NEGATIVE index from the end, so a bare `self.splice(index, 1)[0]` would silently accept exactly the bad index `insert`'s doc says a caller must be punished for. `remove` returns `splice(index, 1)[0]`; `insert` at `len` stays a push. Pin the four bounds cases (`-1`, `len`, `len+1`, and `insert` at `len`) in the corpus beside the existing `List` basics.
